unassigned_checked.why: Checked whether unspecified updates continued season 7; this announces seasons 13/14 and distribution changes, not this story.

persons.name: Amy (brother’s abuse and continuing threats)
persons.harm: Her older brother subjected her to sexual coercion, blackmail, physical injury and intimidation. He murdered their mother and continued threats and attempted recruitment of others to harm Amy from custody.

quotes.quote: And I think that it took me years to even realize that I had been molested by my brother because his hands never touched my body in that way.
And, you know, a lot of times just like abuse happens as the victim, you're, you're felt shameful of it. So you keep it a secret.

contacts.when: Brother about 16–17 onward, recurring for roughly five years
contacts.what_institution_did: Deputies detained him briefly, then released him back home.
contacts.quote: You know, he would get held there in the sheriff's station for a few hours, maybe half a day, a day.
contacts.notes: Mother primarily reported assaults against herself. Sexual abuse of Amy remained concealed. Recurring contacts are not individually datable.

contacts.institution: Police / Men’s Central Jail, Los Angeles
contacts.when: Amy’s college years, about every few months
contacts.what_was_asked: Stop assaults in the family home.
contacts.what_institution_did: Recurring arrests resulted in jail stays of a week to three months.
contacts.quote: You know, there were his jail stints were various lengths. So sometimes he was there for like a week. Sometimes he was there for like three months.

contacts.what_was_asked: Emergency response after brother confessed to killing mother.
contacts.what_institution_did: Warned Amy not to enter because the killer might be inside.
contacts.quote: And I'm opening up our door and she's like, don't go inside. The killer might be inside.
contacts.what_happened_next: She entered, found her mother, and then left.

contacts.what_institution_did: Processed the home, questioned Amy, located the stolen car and captured the offender.
contacts.quote: And finally, the detective came back, and he said, we've got him.
contacts.what_happened_next: He stayed in custody pending proceedings.

contacts.what_institution_did: The process stalled; her share of the estate remained inaccessible pending conviction.
contacts.quote: My 50% share wasn't even freed legally because he hadn't been convicted. So technically because no like judgment had been passed, nobody had any claim yet.
contacts.notes: Repeated lawyer changes and self-representation contributed to delay. Particular estate tribunal and rulings unspecified.

contacts.what_institution_did: Explained that life sentences usually did not result in parole.
contacts.quote: But she explained, and so did the DA, explained to me that the district attorney, that most of the time when life is part of a sentence, people are not given parole.

contacts.what_was_asked: Convict the killer and keep him confined.
contacts.what_institution_did: A plea led to a second-degree murder sentence of 15 years to life.
contacts.quote: I received notice that my brother served 85% of his 15 to life sentence. He was given the ability to see a parole board and be heard for parole.
contacts.what_happened_next: Threats and control continued from custody.
contacts.notes: Not a stated conviction for childhood sexual abuse.

contacts.what_institution_did: Encouraged writing to process her experiences.
contacts.quote: I knew and therapists had suggested, hey, you like words, it gives you catharsis to write, write your book.
contacts.what_happened_next: She wrote a blog and book.
contacts.notes: Support for recovery, distinct from stopping threats.

contacts.what_institution_did: Did not notify her of a transfer.
contacts.quote: He was moved prisons and I didn't know. I wasn't notified.
contacts.what_happened_next: She searched for him and maintained notification-list enrollment.

contacts.when: A Christmas Eve birthday after transfer
contacts.what_was_asked: Information about transfer, infractions and parole.
contacts.what_institution_did: Returned her repeated messages but would not provide the requested information.
contacts.quote: She couldn't even tell me if there were infractions that he had had or faced. All of that is private information.

contacts.what_institution_did: Notified her of the first hearing; subsequently gave August 3 date.
contacts.quote: And then April 16th, 2021, I received notification of my brother's first parole hearing.

contacts.what_institution_did: Approved her for the wrong inmate’s hearing; she identified the error.
contacts.quote: I found that I was approved for the wrong parole board hearing.
contacts.what_happened_next: She ultimately attended the correct hearing.
contacts.notes: Correction evidenced by attendance; no separate correcting response quoted.

contacts.what_institution_did: After the offender threatened the family and made throat-cutting gestures, told Amy to mute and turn off her camera.
contacts.quote: The parole board asked me to mute and turn. turn off my camera at that point, which I did.
contacts.notes: Silencing the threatened person; no explicit attribution of blame is inferred.

contacts.what_was_asked: Respond to threat and hear her statement.
contacts.what_institution_did: Allowed a two-year postponement and offender’s departure; said it would file her statement and give him a transcript.
contacts.quote: And they said, we still have to listen. We will file your statement. He'll get a transcript and he can read it.

contacts.what_institution_did: Notified her of two further prison moves.
contacts.quote: I received an email, two emails actually, the last several months about my brothers being moved prisons.
contacts.notes: No protection or punishment established by transfers themselves.

contacts.when: Repeated calls before Yom Kippur about 15 years after murder
contacts.what_was_asked: Help filing about the threat and obtaining information.
contacts.what_institution_did: Promised callbacks that repeatedly did not occur.
contacts.quote: Leaving messages, the people were saying, oh, well, he said he'd call you back. Sergeant blah, blah, blah, said he'd call you back. Never did.
contacts.what_happened_next: After persistence and mentioning recording future hearings as media, she received more help.

contacts.what_institution_did: Urged continued filings and disclosed an attempted-murder investigation.
contacts.quote: You should keep doing everything you're doing. You have to write all the letters. You have to file everything. But just so you know, your brother's actually under investigation for attempted murder right now.
contacts.what_happened_next: She filed against him for the threat.

contacts.what_was_asked: Recognize the parole statement as a death threat.
contacts.what_institution_did: A written response said the statement did not meet criteria for a threat; gestures and another statement were ignored according to Amy.
contacts.quote: it says although we understand and empathize with you what you've been through and the loss of your mother that statement alone is not suitable and does not meet the criteria for a threat.
contacts.what_happened_next: She later escalated through victim resources.

contacts.what_was_asked: Understand another postponement and family danger.
contacts.what_institution_did: Notified her of postponement and referred her to a superior when unable to answer questions.
contacts.quote: The poor young girl on the phone did not have that information. So she said, I'm gonna put you in touch with my superior.

contacts.what_institution_did: Could not provide more information and escalated to the chief.
contacts.quote: How about I put you in touch with my supervisor as well?
contacts.what_happened_next: She reached the chief of victim resources.

contacts.institution: Chief of victim resources for California prisons
contacts.what_was_asked: Understand new charges and options for protection.
contacts.what_institution_did: Guided her through case records, reporting options, and later supplied the parole transcript.
contacts.quote: This is what you can do. You can file a police report to try to get your brother for this extra crime of the threat. You can try to call the DA on the case, figure out what's happening on the 30th.
contacts.what_happened_next: She obtained records and contacted police and prosecutor.

contacts.what_institution_did: Supplied the prosecutor’s name despite withholding other information.
contacts.quote: I said, well, can I find out the DA's name on the case? She gave it to me.
contacts.what_happened_next: Amy located and contacted the prosecutor.

contacts.what_institution_did: A report was filed and a detective assigned; no further investigative action is described before sentencing.
contacts.quote: I had also filed a police report on March 23rd.
contacts.what_happened_next: She contacted prosecutor directly and later notified detective of conviction.
contacts.notes: Report-taking only is shown; not a claim the report was refused.

contacts.when: Within 24 hours of March 23 contact, then before March 30
contacts.what_institution_did: Reviewed her transcript and preserved letters of attempted hitman recruitment / stalking, and found enough evidence to charge.
contacts.quote: He went on to say, I reviewed the evidence from the hearing, everything. There's absolutely enough evidence to go after him for the death threat.

contacts.what_institution_did: Held a hearing and set a further date after the offender indicated he wanted to plead.
contacts.quote: And the lawyer says to me after the hearing, [perpetrator] is saying he wants to play guilty. This might be all wrapped up. We're going to set another date.

contacts.what_was_asked: Stop recruitment of another inmate to harm her.
contacts.what_institution_did: Arranged separation in custody in response to her request.
contacts.quote: He said, absolutely, he will be solitary so he cannot hire someone to hurt you.

contacts.what_was_asked: Record the hearing as approved media.
contacts.what_institution_did: Denied recording permission, including after prosecutor’s request.
contacts.quote: She said, no, it'll make it a hoopla. I don't want that in my courtroom
contacts.what_happened_next: She attended without permission to record.

contacts.what_institution_did: Brought her and her friend through employee parking and obtained security.
contacts.quote: He drove us from the outside into the employee parking lot, walked us in, got us security.

contacts.institution: Court reporter and bailiffs / Los Angeles County sheriffs
contacts.what_institution_did: Repeatedly shushed and reprimanded Amy and her friend, including outside session.
contacts.quote: Even the court reporter came over at one point and was like, you guys need to be quiet. And we were like, you're not even sending it. You're not typing. We are being quiet.

contacts.what_was_asked: Give her statement despite offender’s attempt to condition his plea.
contacts.what_institution_did: Affirmed her legal right to speak, but did not stop all interruptions and defended the lawyer’s talking.
contacts.quote: The judge says, sir, it's her legal right to make a statement this is not signed and delivered yet but you can't say she can't make a statement she gets to make a statement whether you want her to or not especially if there is a charge for a death threat against her she is technically a victim on file in this situation today so he actually fucking ends up pleading guilty.
contacts.what_happened_next: She completed the statement describing molestation and terror.

contacts.what_institution_did: Imposed six years for family threats and 30 years to life for the officer attack, removed youth-offender status and denied next parole hearing.
contacts.quote: They also gave him 6 years for the death threats against me and my children.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her fear of eventual release substantially diminished.

contacts.what_was_asked: Protection from brother and people acting for him.
contacts.what_institution_did: Initially offered 30 days, then granted a ten-year restraining order after hearing her statement.
contacts.quote: What she offered was a 30 day restraining order. But by the time I had finished my victim impact statement, she said, okay, I'm giving you a 10 year restraining order.
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt freer, though some risk remained.

persons.outcome_quote: he's still in prison, he still abuses me, but I don't have to deal with him anymore
persons.decisive_work_quote: I had those letters. I gave him everything. He went on to say, I reviewed the evidence from the hearing, everything. There's absolutely enough evidence to go after him for the death threat.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: Captured the night of the 2007 murder; elapsed time from first family-violence reports is uncertain. Stronger protection for continuing threats followed approximately three and a half weeks after the March 23, 2023 police report.
persons.notes: Later protection is substantial, including further sentences, third strike and ten-year order. Partly protected because she expressly reports continuing abuse and fear of a hired attacker. Convictions do not establish a childhood sexual-abuse conviction. Early police contacts primarily concerned mother’s assaults; sexual abuse remained concealed. Repeated contacts with no individual dates are grouped rather than invented. Firefighters attending a fire were not told of the coercion, so that attendance is not an institutional abuse contact.

persons.name: Hadas (son’s violence and murder)
persons.harm: Her son repeatedly assaulted and intimidated her, destroyed the home, attacked her with a makeshift flamethrower, and ultimately murdered her with a knife.

contacts.when: Son about 16–17 onward; recurring roughly five years
contacts.what_institution_did: Detained her son briefly and repeatedly released him home.
contacts.quote: So that was about, gosh, five years of just taking him in, and maybe my time is off on that, but five years taking him in, hoping he'll cool down, and then just sending him right back out to us.

contacts.institution: Police responding to makeshift flamethrower attack
contacts.what_institution_did: Police were called; Amy describes them saying they could not help if mother would not maintain charges.
contacts.quote: They had no solutions. They were like, well, that's it. We can't help you.
contacts.notes: Daughter’s understanding of charging requirements; no separate custody outcome specified for this particular attack.

contacts.institution: Police / Men’s Central Jail, Los Angeles
contacts.what_institution_did: Repeated arrests and jail stays temporarily removed him.
contacts.quote: You know, there were his jail stints were various lengths. So sometimes he was there for like a week. Sometimes he was there for like three months.
contacts.what_happened_next: She continued visits and eventually took him back.
contacts.notes: The specific flame attack may overlap this recurring pattern.

contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated and arrested her fleeing killer.
contacts.quote: And finally, the detective came back, and he said, we've got him.

contacts.what_institution_did: A plea resulted in 15 years to life for second-degree murder.
contacts.quote: I received notice that my brother served 85% of his 15 to life sentence. He was given the ability to see a parole board and be heard for parole.
contacts.what_happened_next: He later became eligible for parole.

contacts.what_was_asked: Oppose release and hear family’s account.
contacts.what_institution_did: Allowed postponement and departure, while saying it would file Amy’s statement.
contacts.quote: And they said, we still have to listen. We will file your statement. He'll get a transcript and he can read it.

contacts.institution: Prison crimes judge and district attorney
contacts.what_institution_did: Removed youth-offender status affecting murder parole and denied next parole hearing.
contacts.quote: They went backwards and removed [perpetrator]'s youth offender status. So he is no longer given that benefit

persons.outcome_quote: At this point, she's gone. There's nothing that can bring her back. There's nothing that can make it better.
persons.notes: Also called Dossie / Dassy and other transcript variants. Later convictions are not protection of a person who died from the harm. Accounts from daughter and family friends.

persons.name: Amy (voyeurism by mutual friend)
persons.harm: A mutual friend hid in a closet to watch her have sex without consent; years later a girlfriend disclosed it and told her to take it as a compliment.
persons.outcome_quote: and when my girlfriend told me, she told me I should be, you know, take it as a compliment.
persons.notes: No institutional contact or protection described. Unclear does not assert that no report ever occurred.

persons.name: Amy (restrictive marriage)
persons.harm: Her husband discouraged discussing her mother’s murder and restricted her healing; repeated conflict affected the children. She left and found freedom to write and heal.
persons.outcome_quote: In the moment, I freed myself from that marriage and started focusing more on my own healing in myself. I sold my book, and it was kind of a magical swift process in 2020 while I was stuck at home, I churned it out.
persons.notes: Private separation, not a stated protective institutional response. No divorce-court action is described.

persons.name: Hadas (husband’s mistreatment)
persons.harm: Her husband had affairs, left her for another woman, was largely absent as a parent and evaded child support. Her diary describes feeling used and mistreated.

contacts.when: After separation, before requesting help with son
contacts.what_institution_did: Amy says mother exhausted legal options without securing support; tribunal and individual orders unspecified.
contacts.quote: If she's not even reaching out for money, she had exhausted everything legally.
contacts.what_happened_next: She asked her ex-husband directly and received no help.

persons.outcome_quote: So, and you know, my dad didn't pay child support. He was a lawyer, but he kind of hid his employment a lot.
persons.notes: Diary passages are read on air. Her later death was caused by her son, a separate harm. Legal reach is broadly described, not a reconstructed court history.

persons.name: Hadas (medical injury and denied support)
persons.harm: After an ankle injury, medication around surgery caused an allergic reaction, prolonged vomiting and ruptured discs; she was disabled for years and denied benefits and home nursing.
persons.perpetrator_role: medical providers and unidentified benefits decision-makers

contacts.what_institution_did: Gave medication to which she was allergic; daughter reports vomiting and ruptured discs.
contacts.quote: She fell and tore a couple of ligaments in her, in her ankle and as a result had surgery, but that surgery they gave her a medicine. She was allergic to and she ruptured two discs in her back from throwing up for 18 hours.
contacts.what_happened_next: She was bedbound or wheelchair dependent for about three years.
contacts.notes: Adverse treatment as reported, not adjudicated malpractice or asserted intent.

contacts.what_institution_did: Denied benefits and did not provide a nurse.
contacts.quote: She was denied benefits. She wasn't given a nurse to do basic things.

persons.outcome_quote: She was denied benefits. She wasn't given a nurse to do basic things. She had a hospital bed in our house.
persons.notes: She later returned to teaching, but no remedy for treatment injury or denial is described. Outcome concerns treatment/support harm, not permanent disability. Her son caused her later death.

persons.name: [unnamed] Amy’s friend targeted with lighter
persons.harm: During a visit, Amy’s brother commented on the girl’s body and held a lit lighter under her backside; she told her parents and was forbidden to visit again.
persons.outcome_quote: But I'm my friend was no longer allowed over my house
persons.notes: Parents provided private protection. No institutional response is described. Not assumed to be the named lifelong friend.

persons.name: [unnamed] Arizona girlfriend
persons.harm: Amy describes her brother exploiting and abusing girlfriends. He lived with a serious girlfriend in Arizona, then returned after the relationship failed amid abuse.
persons.outcome_quote: who wants to stand for getting abused physically, emotionally or verbally at all.
persons.notes: Preceding paragraph identifies the Arizona girlfriend. Exact acts against her and institutional contact are unstated. Departure is not institutional protection.

persons.name: [unnamed] Amy’s paternal uncle
persons.harm: He told Amy that her book let him recognize sibling abuse he had suffered from her father.
persons.outcome_quote: Things that you shared and named like sibling abuse was something I faced at the hands of your dad and I didn't even know there was a name for it.
persons.notes: Recognition after reading the book is the stated aftermath. Specific acts, timing, institutional reach and protection unstated; lack of terminology is not inferred to be a reporting-delay reason.

persons.name: [unnamed] attacked correctional officer
persons.harm: An inmate attacked the officer with a homemade mace and shank; other officers intervened and prosecution resulted in a 30-years-to-life sentence.

contacts.what_institution_did: Intervened, with some injured in doing so.
contacts.quote: A bunch of other officers got involved and got hurt in the process of trying to stop my brother.

contacts.when: Before Yom Kippur approximately 15 years after murder
contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated the attack.
contacts.quote: But just so you know, your brother's actually under investigation for attempted murder right now.

contacts.what_institution_did: Pursued five charges including attempted murder, attack on a public official and weapons offenses.
contacts.quote: He was being given one count with five charges for attempted murder, attack on the public official, two weapons charges, and something else I keep forgetting.

contacts.what_institution_did: Accepted plea and imposed 30 years to life for the officer attack.
contacts.quote: He went after him for the five charges against the correctional officer, which he received and took 30 years to life sentence for.

persons.outcome_quote: He went after him for the five charges against the correctional officer, which he received and took 30 years to life sentence for.
persons.decisive_work_quote: A bunch of other officers got involved and got hurt in the process of trying to stop my brother.
persons.notes: Protection includes immediate institutional intervention. Details relayed through Amy’s account of prosecutor’s explanation; recording described but not examined.

persons.name: [unnamed] Amy’s older child (uncle’s threats)
persons.harm: Their uncle threatened the family from prison. The children knew about him and asked whether he would get out; later sentencing let their mother reassure them.

contacts.quote: The parole board asked me to mute and turn. turn off my camera at that point, which I did.

contacts.what_happened_next: Her fear of eventual release substantially diminished.

persons.name: [unnamed] Amy’s older child (marital conflict)
persons.harm: Amy says repeated fights in her marriage affected the children; she left to provide a more peaceful life.
persons.perpetrator_role: their parents in a conflict-filled marriage
persons.outcome_quote: My kids were getting affected by it. And I could see this cycle that wasn't quite what I had been in, but it was still a tumultuous situation, and I knew I wanted more peace and love for my children.
persons.notes: Private separation, not demonstrated institutional protection. No child-directed violence is specified and conflict is not attributed entirely to one parent. Children not individually differentiated.

persons.harm: Amy says repeated fights in her marriage affected the children; she left to provide a more peaceful life.

persons.name: Amy (father’s absence and neglect)
persons.harm: Her father was absent for much of childhood, did not use his custody time and later refused contact when the siblings sought him out.
persons.outcome_quote: I have always called him dad, but he's never been a dad to me.
persons.notes: Custody mentioned without an institutional response to neglect. Father’s police call when approached by siblings did not raise her neglect, so is not such a contact.

persons.name: Amy (school bullying)
